title: score keyword lane classification against a labeled shortlist
summary:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes has a new --labels PATH option. It compares the keyword lane classifier with a hand-labeled JSON file. For each entry it scores title + '. ' + summary using ranked_lanes, whose top lane is the one distill.classify picks. It then applies the existing thin/ambiguous rules. Those rules now live in a flag_reasons helper that inspect() also calls.

The command prints a JSON report with:
- labels: the file's basename only
- labeled and margin
- agreement for all, confident (unflagged) and flagged entries, each as n, agree and rate (rate is null when n is 0)
- disagreements in input order, each with id (null when absent), title, label, predicted, reasons, best and runner_up

A disagreement with reasons [] is a confident misfile that the flags missed.

The whole file is validated before anything is scored. Invalid input exits 2 with one 'lanes: ' stderr line and empty stdout. This covers an unreadable file, invalid JSON or non-UTF-8 text, no items list, a non-object entry, an empty or non-string title or lane, a non-string id or summary, an unknown lane (the valid ids are listed), and combining --labels with --latest or --fail-on-suspicious. In labels mode the exit code is 0 whenever a report is printed. docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 9 documents the format and its limits.

The controller ran the checks, not me. In the pre-feature run, 8 of the 10 feature tests errored because argparse rejected --labels. On candidate c109acf the controller ran python -m pairadar --rerender --no-readme (exit 0), the 10 feature tests (all passed) and the full unittest suite (446 tests, OK).
usage:
Prerequisites: a checkout of this repository, Python 3.12 (the version in the controller's image), no extra packages. Run from the repository root.

1. List the valid lane ids:
python3 -c "from pairadar.config import load_config; print(', '.join(l['id'] for l in load_config().lanes))"

2. Create a SYNTHETIC sample file. The lane values are placeholders, not real human judgments. Replace them with your own labels:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
from pairadar.config import load_config
lanes = [l["id"] for l in load_config().lanes]
items = [
    {"id": "s1", "title": "Control barrier function safety filter with runtime monitor", "summary": "Synthetic example.", "lane": lanes[0]},
    {"title": "Untitled robotics note", "lane": lanes[-1]},
]
with open("my-labels.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    json.dump({"items": items}, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
EOF

3. Score it:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes --labels my-labels.json --margin 0.35

4. Read agreement.all.rate, then compare agreement.confident with agreement.flagged. Look first at disagreements whose reasons is [], because the flags missed those. Edit data/taxonomy.json and re-run on the same file to compare before and after.

5. Error example:
python3 -m pairadar.lanes --labels missing.json
This exits 2 and prints a single 'lanes: cannot read missing.json: ...' line.

Tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_feature_5621e4c46330.py
limitations:
Scope:
- One input format (a JSON items list) and one entry point. --labels combines only with --margin.
- There is no threshold-based failure exit, CSV input, automatic taxonomy editing or model/provider call.
- Classification and scoring are unchanged.

What the numbers mean:
- Labels come from the user.
- The test fixtures and the usage sample are synthetic and labeled as such.
- The passing tests show that the counts, ordering and error handling match hand-computed expectations. They do not show broad classifier accuracy.
- Agreement on a small labeled set measures the current taxonomy on those items only. It is not general accuracy, and the margin is not calibrated.
- Keep the labeled set separate from the examples used to tune keywords.

Verification gaps:
- This is a CLI-only feature. No browser or visual review of it was done, and I did not check whether the full suite includes browser or showcase tests.
- An earlier review flagged unrelated banner SVG coordinate changes and a CHANGELOG file-list claim. The controller receipts do not include the final diff's file list, and I could not inspect it. So this text makes no claim about which files the commit touches beyond the lanes feature.
- The rerender check exiting 0 does not prove that assets are unchanged.
- Issue #73 is not addressed.
upgrade:
Additive. Without --labels, the existing command and its --latest, --margin and --fail-on-suspicious options keep their output and exit codes. The --latest default now resolves internally to the same radar/latest.json path. inspect() now calls the extracted flag_reasons helper, which uses the same rules. Label files are only read, and the feature adds no stored data or schema.

To roll back, revert the feature commit. Label files are user-owned and stay intact. Before releasing, confirm the commit's file list matches the lanes feature (see limitations).

title: choose the content gaps period and export the same window
summary:
The Content gaps card on the Conversations screen now has a Period control with Last 7 days, Last 30 days and Last 90 days, plus a Show button. The form does not submit when the select changes. After Show, the summary sentence, the gap table and the empty state cover the chosen window. The empty state names the window and suggests trying a longer period.

The period carries over to the Stored exchanges filter, pagination and the Reset link. Reset clears only the log search, source and rating. At 30 days, including when invalid input falls back to 30, none of those forms or URLs gain aicfab_gap_days, and Reset is the plain page URL, as in 1.47.6.

Download content gaps CSV exports the window shown on screen. Seven-day and 90-day files are named ai-chat-bedrock-content-gaps-7d-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.csv and ...-90d-.... A 30-day file, or one with a missing or rejected period, keeps the legacy name. The columns are unchanged.

The new AI_Chat_Bedrock_Insights::gap_window() accepts only an int, or a string of digits alone, equal to 7, 30 or 90. Anything else returns 30. The export handler reads the period only after the manage_options and nonce checks. The version is 1.48.0.

The controller ran the checks on commit f279e41. The feature test failed on the base commit, which lacks the feature, and passed on the candidate. On the candidate, bin/prerelease.sh passed: 40 suites, including admin-ux.php, insights.php and the earlier content-gap test test_feature_9ecd4de5ba50.php, which had failed in the prior attempt; phpcs was clean across 75 files. tests/tooling.php and bin/build-package.py also passed (89 files).
usage:
Prerequisites: a WordPress 6.4+ site on PHP 7.4+ with plugin 1.48.0 active, conversation logging turned on in Settings, and a user with manage_options.

1. Create sample input (manual, synthetic). In the site's public chat, ask two questions the site has no content for, for example "What payload can the demo robot arm lift?" twice. Each question needs at least 8 characters. Each is logged as an ungrounded exchange.
2. Go to WP Admin, AI Chat for Amazon Bedrock, Conversations.
3. In the Content gaps card, set Period to Last 7 days and press Show. The summary and table now cover 7 days. Filtering or paging the Stored exchanges log keeps the period.
4. Press Download content gaps CSV. The file is named like ai-chat-bedrock-content-gaps-7d-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.csv and has the columns question, occurrences, last_asked_utc, grounded_count and ungrounded_count.

From code, for example with WP-CLI:
wp eval 'var_dump( AI_Chat_Bedrock_Insights::gap_window( "90" ), AI_Chat_Bedrock_Insights::gap_window( "7\n" ) );'
This prints int(90) and int(30).
wp eval 'echo AI_Chat_Bedrock_Insights::export_filename( 7, 0 );'
This prints ai-chat-bedrock-content-gaps-7d-19700101-000000.csv.

Repository checks, run from the plugin root:
php -d zend.assertions=1 -d assert.exception=1 tests/test_feature_ed4081b0c575.php
bash bin/prerelease.sh --php /usr/bin/php
limitations:
Only 7, 30 and 90 days are offered. There are no custom date ranges and no saved or per-user preference. Gap grouping, the full-conversation Export CSV, CLI and REST are unchanged.

Conversation retention and the MAX_ENTRIES log cap still limit how far back a window reaches. On short-retention sites, 90 days can show the same result as 30.

The rendered-HTML checks run the real partial against stubbed WordPress functions, with synthetic seeded entries. The controller's run did not include WordPress Plugin Check or live integration (no --wp-cli was given), nor any browser, screenshot or real-WordPress run for this feature. The 360px wrapping, focus rings and overall look are inferred from the flex-wrap rule and core admin classes; they were not visually verified. bin/audit-accessibility.py remains a manual check against a live site.

Passing tests show that the window, URLs and file names behave as specified. They do not show that the gap grouping is accurate for any particular site. The checks ran on PHP 8.4.26; PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.4 support is the plugin's stated floor and was not re-run here.
upgrade:
Update to 1.48.0. There is no migration and there are no new options: the period exists only in the request.

The default 30-day view, the log filter, pagination and Reset URLs, the CSV columns, and the file name for a download with no period or an invalid one are the same as in 1.47.6. Only 7-day and 90-day downloads get -7d- or -90d- in the name, so any script that collects these files by the legacy pattern should also allow that segment.

To roll back, reinstall 1.47.6. The control disappears, any leftover aicfab_gap_days parameter in bookmarks is ignored, and no stored conversations, ratings or settings change in either direction.

title: Decision coverage for recorded choices
summary: How often does a recorded choice component answer when it abstains below a confidence threshold, and how often is it wrong? EvalArc 0.16.0 chooses the threshold on calibration decisions, then reports coverage and selective error on held-out decisions. Invalid responses stay visible instead of being counted as wrong answers.
usage:
python -m pip install evalarc==0.16.0
evalarc decision-coverage RECORDS.json --max-error 0.2 --output runs/decision-review
# Open runs/decision-review/index.html; the release guide has a synthetic input example.
limitations: This reviews saved choice decisions only. The bundled example is synthetic and says nothing about a provider’s accuracy. Reported confidence is not calibrated by this command. The new HTML report passed structure and escaping tests; its layout and keyboard behavior were not checked in a real browser.
upgrade: Install EvalArc 0.16.0 to add this command. Reinstall 0.15.0 to roll back; existing inputs and generated reports are left alone.

title: Check a skill choice against the installed shortlist
summary: Skills Anywhere 0.16.0 adds a two-step route command. Prepare builds a shortlist of installed skills that can actually be opened; apply checks a saved choice against that shortlist before it is used. The result says whether the pick is selected, absent, below the confidence threshold, stale or invalid. The command does not load or run the skill.
usage:
npm install -g dsh-skills-anywhere@0.16.0
dsh-skills-anywhere route prepare "fill PDF forms" --json > request.json
# Save the recorded choice as response.json, then check it:
dsh-skills-anywhere route apply --request request.json --response response.json
limitations: The route command is CLI-only and checks installed skills on the current machine. Its default confidence threshold of 0.7 is a user-set cutoff, not evidence that any classifier is calibrated. Preparing or applying a route does not execute a skill or send it over the network.
upgrade: Install dsh-skills-anywhere 0.16.0 for the new route command. Reinstall 0.15.0 to roll back; saved request and response JSON files remain untouched.

title: stall-threshold sensitivity for recorded step-limit failures
summary: Adds --stall-sweep T1,T2,... to python -m robot_reel.stress. It re-labels verified recorded step-limit traces at up to eight stall thresholds in metres and reports per-threshold counts, changed and stable trials, and threshold-dependent boundaries against the unchanged 1 mm reference. No policy is re-run and no threshold is validated.
usage:
python3 -m robot_reel.stress docs/stress --reliability --stall-sweep 0.0005,0.002,0.005

The collection is verified first. Then the JSON output gains stall_sensitivity with these fields: schema, trials, reference_threshold_m (0.001), thresholds (sorted, reference included), by_threshold (counts and stalled_trials per threshold), changed (per non-reference threshold: trial, reference_kind, kind, tail_travel_m), step_limit_trials, stable_step_limit_trials, boundary (per step-limit trial: tail_travel_m, kinds per threshold, depends_on_threshold) and scope. Invalid input such as --stall-sweep=2 exits with status 2 and prints a message like: --stall-sweep value '2' exceeds 1 m; thresholds are metres of end-effector travel, not millimetres.
limitations: CLI-only; there is no UI change, so no browser or visual checks apply. The sweep describes label sensitivity on the recorded traces, using tail travel over the final tenth of frames as the only motion measure. It does not choose, calibrate or statistically test a threshold, and it does not re-run policies. The behavioral tests use labeled synthetic traces through the real CLI. For those tests, collection verification and loading are patched to stand in for a verified collection. A separate test checks the sweep's reference threshold against the sealed reliability.json of the published collection. The published reliability.json, the summary, the manifests and verify_site are unchanged. I did not run the tests in this environment.
upgrade: Upgrade to the release containing this change. The change adds one optional flag and one new output key, so existing commands, published packs and schemas keep working without migration. To roll back, revert the commit or reinstall the previous version. No stored artifact depends on stall_sensitivity.

title: report consecutive-failure streak and failing_since date for struggling sources in pairadar.health
summary: `python3 -m pairadar.health` now tells the maintainer and the nightly repair gate whether a struggling source has been continuously dark or is flapping. Each entry under `struggling` gains two fields next to the existing `source` and `failed_days`: `streak_days`, the number of consecutive runs (counted back from the latest run that recorded health inside the window) on which the source appears in `failed`, and `failing_since`, the `date` of the oldest run in that streak. A run on which the source answered, was served by its fallback endpoint, or was not attempted ends the streak. A new public helper `health.streak(runs, reference, window, source)` returns `(streak_days, failing_since)` and `(0, None)` when the source did not fail the latest run. All previously emitted keys (`reference`, `window_days`, `threshold_days`, `runs_with_health`, `failures`, `fallbacks`, and `source`/`failed_days` inside `struggling`), the worst-first ranking, the threshold and latest-run rules, and `--fail-on-struggling` exit codes are unchanged. The module docstring and docs/automation.md explain the two fields.
usage:
python3 -m pairadar.health --date 2026-09-27
# {
#   "reference": "2026-09-27",
#   "window_days": 14,
#   "threshold_days": 3,
#   "runs_with_health": 6,
#   "failures": {"ieee-spectrum": 5},
#   "fallbacks": {},
#   "struggling": [
#     {"source": "ieee-spectrum", "failed_days": 5, "streak_days": 5, "failing_since": "2026-09-23"}
#   ]
# }

# From Python:
from datetime import date
from pairadar import health
runs = health.load_runs()
print(health.streak(runs, date(2026, 9, 27), health.WINDOW, "ieee-spectrum"))  # (5, '2026-09-23')

# Tests:
python3 -m unittest tests.test_feature_644be79e9748
limitations: Streaks count consecutive runs that recorded health, not calendar days: if the publisher skipped a day, the gap is invisible and the streak continues across it. `failing_since` is bounded by the window, so an outage older than `--window` reports the oldest run inside the window (with `--window 3` a six-day outage shows `streak_days: 3`). Fallback-served runs are not failures and end the streak, matching the existing policy. No new CLI flags; fetch.py, the history.json schema, the repair job's trigger condition and `--fail-on-struggling` semantics are unchanged. Not covered: per-source item counts, feeds that answer but publish nothing, alerting, or the published site. Standard library only, Python 3.9+ as before (`from __future__ import annotations` is already in the module).
upgrade: Additive change to pairadar/health.py (one new function, two new fields per struggling entry, one docstring paragraph), one new test file tests/test_feature_644be79e9748.py, and three lines in docs/automation.md. radar/history.json is only read; no data files are rewritten. Upgrade by pulling the commit; consumers that parse the health JSON keep working because no existing key changes name or value. Rollback is `git revert` of the single commit, which removes the two fields, the helper and the test with no data loss.

title: content-gap insight export as CSV for editorial workflow
summary: Export ranked content gaps as CSV for editorial planning.
usage: WordPress admin → AI Chat for Amazon Bedrock → Conversations → Content gaps → Download content gaps CSV.
limitations: Administrator access is required. Includes up to 15 ranked groups from the last 30 days of retained exchanges; list filters do not apply. Counts cover gap-contributing exchanges, not all answers. An empty report contains only the header. The CSV contains visitor questions.
upgrade: Update to 1.47.0 using the WordPress plugin updater or the release ZIP. Back up the site before upgrading; retain the previous plugin package and backup for rollback. Logging and retention settings continue to apply.
